name: Normal AWS service trust (lambda.amazonaws.com) - informational only, never external/escalation
note: IAM-805 negative control (acceptance-suite test 18). A service principal assuming the role is a standard service-role relationship. The analyzer emits at most an informational TRUST-SERVICE relationship and NEVER a public/external/escalation finding, and NEVER infers the assumed role's permissions from the trust policy alone.
rationale: AWS documents a service principal (Principal.Service, e.g. lambda.amazonaws.com) in a role trust policy as a normal service-role relationship: the named AWS service may assume the role to act on the account's behalf (trust-policy-semantics 2.5). It is neither an external-account principal nor anonymous, so no PUBLIC-TRUST, cross-account, org-expansion, or federated-subject finding applies. Critically, a trust policy conveys WHO MAY ASSUME the role, never the assumed role's permissions - so no escalation path or privilege inference is licensed by the trust document alone (the negative control, acceptance test 18). Emitting anything above informational, or any identity-style broad-Resource finding, would overstate the evidence (threat-model T8). Ref: AWS Principal element (Service); docs/trust-policy-semantics.md sec 2.5 and 5 (service trust = informational).
